anchors.paper_title: Undivided attention: The temporal effects of attention dissociated from decision, memory, and expectation
anchors.reason: The dataset README cites this preprint as its study paper. Its title and abstract describe the same 20-participant EEG study with oriented gratings, attention and temporal expectation, and the authors match.

metadata.methods_description: EEG was recorded from 20 participants during a session of about 1 hour. Participants viewed rapid sequences of overlaid oriented gratings, attended one colour-cued grating while ignoring the other, and detected a target orientation. Stimulus onset timing was either predictable or unpredictable.

citation_details.title: An empirically-driven guide on using Bayes Factors for M/EEG decoding
citation_details.author: Lina Teichmann, Denise Moerel, Chris I. Baker, Tijl Grootswagers
citation_details.abstract: Bayes factors can be used to provide quantifiable evidence for contrasting hypotheses and have thus become increasingly popular in cognitive science. However, Bayes factors are rarely used to statistically assess the results of neuroimaging experiments. Here, we provide an empirically driven guide on implementing Bayes factors for time-series neural decoding results. Using real and simulated magnetoencephalography (MEG) data, we examine how parameters such as the shape of the prior and data size affect Bayes factors. Additionally, we discuss the benefits Bayes factors bring to analysing multivariate pattern analysis data and show how using Bayes factors can be used instead or in addition to traditional frequentist approaches.
